overview: AI agents and scaling methods dominate research focus
OpenAI’s branding and policy moves signal political engagement
Tech CEOs face criticism for AI optimism

top.title: Agentic World Modeling for Agent Test-time Scaling without Environment Replica
top.summary: The paper proposes Agentic World Modeling, enabling agents to scale test-time performance without replicating environments, by learning world models that generalize across tasks. This could reduce reliance on costly environment simulations for AI development.

top.title: OpenAI might rebrand its data centers as ‘AI compute campuses’
top.summary: OpenAI is considering rebranding its data centers as “AI compute campuses” and launching a PR campaign ahead of the 2028 election, promoting AI policy ideas like speed limits and global standards to shape public debate.

top.title: Towards Portable Specification of the Agent Harness
top.summary: The work introduces a portable specification for the Agent Harness, a framework to standardize how AI agents are defined, deployed, and evaluated, aiming to improve reproducibility and interoperability across research labs.

top.title: Muse AI agent is a commercial surveillance network disguised as an AI assistant
top.summary: A Hacker News post highlights Muse AI, an agent marketed as an assistant but operating as a commercial surveillance network, raising concerns about privacy and the misuse of AI under the guise of productivity tools.

top.title: AI Can Write More of the Code. We Still Have to Engineer the System
top.summary: An essay argues that AI can automate code implementation but not design or decision‑making, emphasizing the need for engineers to retain responsibility, maintain transparent documentation, and address continuity challenges in long‑running AI agents.

top.title: AI can make tech CEOs’ lives easier. What about everyone else?
top.summary: TechCrunch discusses criticism of CEOs like Marissa Mayer, Sam Altman, and Mark Zuckerberg for promoting AI as a personal‑life solution, suggesting a disconnect between executive messaging and broader public concerns about AI’s societal impact.
